title: Forensic snapshot rotation contract (L19)
description: Invariants for MAGMA L4 forensic-snapshot rotation. See ADR-022.

invariants.name: raw_chain_authoritative
invariants.description: Raw MAGMA event chain is the source of truth. Snapshots are derived. On hash mismatch between snapshot and raw chain, raw chain wins.
must: hash mismatch logs WARNING and falls back to raw-chain walk

invariants.name: snapshot_boundary_hash
invariants.description: Every snapshot stores hash of raw event at the snapshot boundary. Replay verifies the hash before trusting the snapshot.
must: replay verifies boundary_event_hash == raw chain hash at that index

invariants.name: fail_closed_fallback
invariants.description: Snapshot read failure (disk, corruption, hash mismatch) MUST fall back to raw-chain walk with a logged WARNING. No silent skip.
must: ENOENT on snapshot file -> WARNING + raw walk
ChecksumError on snapshot -> WARNING + raw walk
snapshot id is logged in fallback path

invariants.name: replay_equivalence
invariants.description: Replay-from-snapshot + delta MUST produce the same observable state as raw-chain walk for the same event range.
must: for any snapshot S and event range [S.boundary, end]: replay(S, delta) == replay_raw(start, end)
tested with property-style equivalence on small synthetic chains

invariants.name: no_write_amplification
invariants.description: Snapshot generation is read-only from the raw chain. No reordering, no rewrites.
must: MagmaSnapshotEngine has no write API to raw chain
snapshot records have separate storage path from raw events

invariants.name: rotation_is_policy_not_code
invariants.description: Rotation cadence, retention window, and tier-transition thresholds are operator-configurable via configs/forensic_snapshots.yaml. No magic numbers in code.
must: configs/forensic_snapshots.yaml is the single source for rotation policy
code reads rotation_interval_hours, warm_retention_count, cold_after_days from config
default values documented in YAML, not hardcoded in Python

out_of_scope: Snapshot-driven incremental retraining of L1/L2/L3 caches (separate ADR)
